rationale: All 30 isolated turntable views and 30 in-hand actor/tool/target views were inspected across front, rear, left, right, three-quarter, overhead and detail angles.

The axe, pickaxe and pry tool have visible authored blue/orange/brown finish; no white silhouette, debug primitive, reversed attachment, floating grip, body penetration or missed contact was observed.
Cross-view silhouettes, material boundaries, intentional hand/tool gaps and native-4K contact remain coherent.
The four automatic contextual loops preserve Havenline's authored stylized material language and physical actor-source-transfer-carry chain.
All 24 device pixels show one movement joystick and zero action buttons; no pickup, tool-cycle, gather or inventory button appears.
The selected-source ring, resource-specific tool, impact response, one-unit transfer and physical carried destination are readable without introducing out-of-scope systems.
All 32 static resource states and all eight sequence videos were inspected for approach, focus, contact, recovery, cancel, re-entry, depletion and respawn.
Every source has exactly two authoritative commits: units 2 to 1/inventory 0 to 1, then units 1 to 0/inventory 1 to 2. Maximum simultaneous transfer flight and impact pulse are each one.
Settled depletion shows zero source units, hidden source and tool, empty action identity, zero flights and zero pulses; respawn is visibly distinct and restores harvestable presentation.

The character-rigging critic protocol was applied to the full real-time and true 0.25x slow-review chop, mine and dismantle cycles, transitions, nine turn angles and five close-contact views per action.
Real/slow frame counts are 29/112 chop, 32/124 mine and 34/131 dismantle. Slow durations are approximately 3.86 times real durations, confirming genuine quarter-speed review evidence.

All 27 turns, 15 close contacts and every cycle contact window are contact-ready and aligned with sub-micrometre recorded impact/grip error. Feet/toes/knees/hips, shoulders/elbows/hands, cuffs, boots, belt/pouches, hem, tool grip and target contact remain stable with no visible loop pop or clipping.
Exact-base and candidate used the same forced-render script at 3840x2160 after 30 warm-up frames for 180 measured active-harvest frames on llvmpipe.

Candidate deltas: p95 -62.225 ms, p99 -500.047 ms, average draw calls +2, average primitives -330.511, static memory +1.054 MB, visible materials +2, shaders/physics/animation/population +0. All declared limits pass.

Maximum runtime fragments and impact pulses are zero after settling and unchanged active-state node count is stable. Thermal score applies only to the bounded software preflight; physical 4K60 and thermal certification remain explicitly outside T09.
